title: Component Chemistry: Usage Guardrails & Migration Scenarios for Tokens, Controls, and Data Views
creator: Noah Chen
description: Purpose: Deliver a compact, example-first documentation update that clarifies how design tokens interact with core controls (buttons, inputs), layout primitives (tables), and visualization components (charts). Focus is on: 1) concrete do/don't examples that capture common integration errors (token misuse, spacing collapse, color contrast regressions), 2) migration scenarios for teams moving from legacy tokens to token v2, 3) API surface notes with recommended shorthand patterns, and 4) accessibility guardrails and measurable checks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Publish a doc page for each surface: Tokens -> Controls -> Tables -> Charts with at least 3 do/don't examples each.
2) Include a migration appendix with a step-by-step script and GitHub link for automated token replacement.
3) All code examples compile in the Storybook sandbox and include Jest/axe test snippets for one representative example per component.
4) Design sign-off from PM and Engineering (comments thread resolved).
5) Published page includes links to related rollout checklist and a short changelog entry for docs-2026.03 release.

notes: Design decisions and trade-offs: prefer explicit token usage over implicit CSS fallbacks to reduce accidental contrast regressions; provide quick migration path but recommend staged rollout (canary by route). Trade-off: more docs vs. developer friction during migration — mitigation: provide a CLI/PR helper to automate changes and preview diffs.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish docs in internal docs site and Storybook behind a feature flag. 2) Run migration-script-stub in a test repo to collect patterns and edge-cases. 3) Release migration helper CLI (minor semver) and announce in #platform-dev. 4) After 2 weeks and no major blockers, flip feature flag and promote to main docs site.
example_snippets:
Do: Use semantic token 'bg-surface' for card backgrounds so theme swaps behave predictably.
Code: <Card style={{ background: tokens.bgSurface }} />

Don't: Hardcode hex colors for hover state on a button — this bypasses theming and contrast checks.
Bad: .btn:hover { background: #f5c; }
Migration tip: CLI command: yarn ds-migrate --from=legacy-tokens --to=token-v2 --dry-run > migration-diff.patch
